findings.title: Identity Audit 'Actor' column is fabricated from the query filter
findings.observedBehaviour: The projection sets actorUserId: q.subjectUserId ?? null. With no subjectUserId filter every row carries null and the page renders 'System'. With ?subjectUserId=<X> every row instead claims X as the actor, whoever really acted.
findings.expectedBehaviour: The Actor column shows the user who performed the event, or an explicit 'unknown' when attribution was never recorded.
findings.codeEvidence: admin-identity.routes.ts:1055 `actorUserId: q.subjectUserId ?? null`; page.tsx:275 `actorType: e.actorUserId ? "HUMAN" : "SYSTEM"` launders 'unknown' into 'System' even though presentActor (apps/web/lib/audit/auditPresentation.ts:106-125) has a correct UNKNOWN_LEGACY branch.
findings.runtimeEvidence: GET /v1/admin/identity/timeline?teamId=<northwind>&limit=5 -> every row actorUserId=null. Same query with &subjectUserId=0adf...0002 -> the identical rows return actorUserId=0adf...0002. The sso_health_checked row was in fact performed by 0adf...0001.
findings.rootCause: The route projects the request filter instead of the stored actor. The writer (identity-operations-completion.routes.ts:464) records the actor only inside the details JSONB, never in the queryable SecurityEvent.userId column, so no correct value is available to project either.
findings.operatorRisk: The surface an operator opens to answer 'who changed our SSO' answers with a value derived from their own filter. On this fixture 100% of rows attribute to 'System'.
findings.securityRisk: Audit-integrity: a compliance timeline that misattributes actions cannot support an investigation or an access review.
findings.recommendedFix: Persist the acting user in SecurityEvent.userId at write time and project that column. Keep presentActor's UNKNOWN_LEGACY branch for historical rows rather than defaulting them to SYSTEM.
findings.dependency: Requires a backfill decision for existing rows whose actor lives only in details.actorUserId.
findings.blastRadius: One route projection plus the emit sites that omit userId.
findings.acceptanceProof: GET the timeline with and without subjectUserId; the actor of a known event is the same in both, and equals the user who performed it.
evidenceNotes: admin-identity.routes.ts and auditPresentation.ts are byte-identical on the completion baseline.

findings.title: Effective-retention resolver returns 500 on its default call path
findings.observedBehaviour: Unless evidenceType, jurisdiction AND caseId are all supplied the query includes an OR arm { id: "__never__" }. `id` is @db.Uuid, so Prisma rejects the whole query with P2007 and the API answers 500 DATABASE_ERROR, additionally emitting an operational.alert at severity 'critical'.
findings.expectedBehaviour: A resolver called with no optional scope filters returns the workspace-level decision.
findings.codeEvidence: retention-engine.service.ts:578,586,594 `{ id: "__never__" }`; services/api/prisma/schema.prisma:8841 `id String @id ... @db.Uuid`.
findings.runtimeEvidence: ?teamId=<t> -> 500; ?teamId=<t>&evidenceType=PHOTO -> 500; ?teamId=<t>&evidenceType=PHOTO&jurisdiction=EU&caseId=<uuid> -> 200 {"policy":null,"reason":"no_active_policy"}. API log: prismaCode P2007, model EvidenceRetentionPolicy, then reason api_5xx_response severity critical.
findings.rootCause: A sentinel chosen as an impossible string is not type-valid for a UUID column, so it invalidates the query rather than matching nothing.
findings.operatorRisk: The governance page's effective-retention panel never resolves on the default view; each load raises a critical operational alert, training operators to ignore that alert class.
findings.securityRisk: None directly; the UI does render a safe failure card rather than a false answer.
findings.recommendedFix: Build the OR array by pushing only the arms whose input is present, instead of emitting an impossible-id no-op arm.
findings.blastRadius: One service function; every caller of resolveEffectiveRetentionPolicy.
findings.acceptanceProof: GET the endpoint with teamId only and receive 200, and no api_5xx_response alert in the log for that request.
evidenceNotes: retention-engine.service.ts unchanged; the '__never__' UUID sentinel is still present at lines 578/586/594.

findings.title: Eleven /admin pages are customer-tenant administration under a Platform-Admin URL and gate
findings.roleCapability: page gate requiredCapabilities [PLATFORM_ADMIN] + requiredActiveSpace PLATFORM_ADMIN; APIs require only tenant membership
findings.endpoint: 37 of 74 param-free GET endpoints reachable from /admin are platform; 32 are ordinary tenant endpoints
findings.observedBehaviour: Every param-free GET these pages make is callable by an ordinary organization owner, and the platform-admin capability grants no cross-tenant reach: for a workspace the operator is not a member of, /v1/admin/identity/* answers 404 for the platform admin while answering 200 for that workspace's own owner.
findings.expectedBehaviour: /admin is the Platform Admin console; a page under it administers the platform or a named tenant chosen by the operator, not the operator's own workspace.
findings.codeEvidence: requireIdentityAdmin resolves prisma.teamMember for the caller and returns 404 when absent; it never consults resolvePlatformAdmin. The eleven pages all read useTeamId() (the operator's own active workspace).
findings.runtimeEvidence: Cross-tenant matrix: /v1/admin/identity/providers?teamId=<Quiet Chambers> -> platform-admin 404, org-owner (that tenant's owner) 200. Same for scim/tokens and timeline. probe-admin-split: 32 endpoints reachable by org-owner, 37 refused to org-owner.
findings.rootCause: The pages were built inside the platform console but bound to the operator's active workspace, so the URL and the gate describe an audience the code never had.
findings.operatorRisk: A genuine platform operator who is not a member of a customer workspace cannot use these pages for any customer; they silently administer the operator's own workspace instead.
findings.securityRisk: None observed: the backend is tenant-correct and the frontend gate is stricter than the API. The risk is comprehension, not access.
findings.recommendedFix: Owner decision PV-OD-001. Either move them to a workspace/organization family, or keep them and add an explicit tenant selector so /admin means 'the platform, or a tenant I have chosen'.
findings.dependency: PV-DUP-001 — the same capability is already reachable outside /admin.
findings.blastRadius: 11 pages, their navigation entries, breadcrumbs, and the adminScopeDispositions register.
findings.acceptanceProof: For each page, either the operator can pick which tenant it administers, or the route no longer sits under /admin.
evidenceNotes: STRENGTHENED. The completion pass adds the organization dimension: a platform admin — whether or not they are a member of a customer WORKSPACE — receives 403/404 on every /v1/orgs/:id endpoint. Platform authority grants no reach at organization level either, so the eleven pages are tenant administration on both axes.

findings.title: A refused Resolve reports the wrong reason for one of the two refusal codes
findings.observedBehaviour: The backend refuses with two distinct codes — CONDITION_STILL_ACTIVE and CONDITION_NOT_DIRECTLY_RESOLVABLE — and the UI shows one message for both: 'Its source still reports it as live, so the platform declined to close it.' That sentence is false for CONDITION_NOT_DIRECTLY_RESOLVABLE, where the condition has no direct remediation at all.
findings.expectedBehaviour: Each refusal code produces its own operator-facing sentence.
findings.codeEvidence: page.tsx:277-279 supplies a single fallback message for action === 'resolve'; the API sends message 'Incident action refused' plus the discriminating code.
findings.runtimeEvidence: Executing Resolve on one incident of each kind: IDENTITY_SECURITY 200 (OPERATOR_DECISION), REPORT 200 (SOURCE_TRUTH), RECONCILIATION 409 CONDITION_STILL_ACTIVE, EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY 409 CONDITION_STILL_ACTIVE, WORKER 409 CONDITION_NOT_DIRECTLY_RESOLVABLE.
findings.rootCause: toSafeUserError is given one fallback per action rather than per refusal code.
findings.operatorRisk: An operator is told to wait for a source to clear when in fact no remediation exists, so they retry indefinitely.
findings.recommendedFix: Map the two codes to two sentences; for NOT_DIRECTLY_RESOLVABLE say that the condition cannot be closed by hand and point at the runbook.
findings.blastRadius: One error handler.
findings.acceptanceProof: Resolving a WORKER 'Unclassified security signal' shows a message that does not claim the source is still live.
evidenceNotes: remediation-executor.ts CHANGED in ec92bc6a (artifact-regeneration outcome mapping). Retested: both refusal codes still reachable — 'Search index reconciliation failing' and 'Trusted timestamping failed' return CONDITION_STILL_ACTIVE, 'Worker heartbeat stale' returns CONDITION_NOT_DIRECTLY_RESOLVABLE — and the UI still shows one message for both. Finding stands unchanged.

findings.title: Forty-three visible disabled controls across twenty-six routes offer no reason
findings.observedBehaviour: 43 controls are rendered disabled with neither a title nor an aria-describedby. The same console does this well elsewhere — SCIM's 'New token' carries title='Issuing a token is part of the Enterprise plan. Existing tokens can still be revoked.' — so the omission is inconsistency, not an absent pattern.
findings.expectedBehaviour: Every disabled control states why, adjacently and accessibly.
findings.codeEvidence: 557 `disabled=` attributes across the in-scope tree; the rendered subset without a reason is 43.
findings.runtimeEvidence: Worst offenders: /organizations/:id/setup 6, /governance-platform/access-reviews 4, /governance-platform/policies 3, /admin/customers 2, /admin/users 2, /admin/workspaces 2, /admin/evidence-ops/records 2, /admin/identity/timeline 2, /governance/policy 2, /organizations/:id/admin/bulk-invite 2.
findings.rootCause: No shared contract requiring a reason alongside `disabled`.
findings.operatorRisk: An operator cannot tell a missing permission from a missing plan from a missing prerequisite.
findings.recommendedFix: Require a reason wherever `disabled` is set on an interactive control, and add a render-time guard.
findings.blastRadius: 26 routes.
findings.acceptanceProof: A DOM sweep finds zero visible disabled controls without title or aria-describedby.
evidenceNotes: Extended by PV-DIS-003 with three further named controls found on the Enterprise surfaces.

findings.title: Audit event labels are generated by mechanical title-casing, mangling 104 of 382 event types
findings.observedBehaviour: humaniseEventType does eventType.replace(/_/g,' ').replace(/\b\w/g, c=>c.toUpperCase()). Every word is capitalised, so acronyms become Sso, Scim, Saml, Mfa, Rbac, Sla. 104 of the 382 SECURITY_EVENT_TYPES contain such an acronym. There is no curated label catalog.
findings.expectedBehaviour: Curated product labels ('SSO health checked'), with the technical identifier available as secondary detail.
findings.codeEvidence: The function's own comment says 'snake_case -> "Snake case"' while the code title-cases every word — the comment and the behaviour disagree.
findings.runtimeEvidence: GET timeline returns summary 'Sso Health Checked' for eventType sso_health_checked.
findings.rootCause: A generated label was used where a curated vocabulary is needed.

findings.title: The fixture launcher's isolation does not cover the API's own .env loader, so a local run holds production secrets
findings.audience: engineers, CI, anyone running the local fixture
findings.observedBehaviour: The fixture environment is built from an allowlist and additionally sets DOTENV_CONFIG_PATH to a non-existent file, with the comment 'so services/api/.env cannot fill a variable this allowlist happens not to set'. That guard targets `import "dotenv/config"`, which services/api/src no longer imports anywhere. The loader the API actually runs is env.ts's own readFileSync loader, which reads <cwd>/.env, services/api/.env and the repo-root .env and fills every variable still undefined. It never consults DOTENV_CONFIG_PATH. The one switch that would stop it, PROOVRA_ENV_BOOTSTRAPPED, is set only by the test bootstrap and by neither fixture launcher.
findings.expectedBehaviour: A fixture process holds only the allowlisted environment. Any variable outside the allowlist stays undefined.
findings.codeEvidence: env.ts lines 65-71 call loadEnvFile(cwdEnv), loadEnvFile(serviceEnv), loadEnvFile(repoRootEnv); `grep -c DOTENV_CONFIG_PATH services/api/src/env.ts` returns 0; `grep -rn 'dotenv/config' services/api/src` returns only comments describing its REMOVAL. TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID does not appear in scripts/local-fixture-env/index.mjs.
findings.runtimeEvidence: The same launcher at the same commit, in two worktrees. In D:/digital-witness, which contains services/api/.env, the startup snapshot reports communications.twilio {configured: true}. In D:/pv-audit-completion, which has no .env, the same snapshot reports {configured:false, reason:'missing:TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID,TWILIO_API_KEY,TWILIO_API_SECRET'}. Nothing else differs.
findings.rootCause: A mitigation written against the loader the code used at the time, left in place after the loader was replaced.
findings.operatorRisk: None for customers; this is a developer-tooling boundary.
findings.securityRisk: A local fixture run holds every production credential in services/api/.env that the allowlist does not overwrite — Twilio, Resend, Sentry, OpenAI and anything else in that file. The allowlist DOES pin DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL and S3, so storage and data stayed local, and every integration flag is off, so nothing outbound fired. The exposure is possession, not use. This also qualifies the previous audit's isolation statement, which is corrected in this pass.
findings.recommendedFix: Set PROOVRA_ENV_BOOTSTRAPPED=1 in buildLocalFixtureEnv. It is the switch env.ts already honours, it needs no new mechanism, and it makes allowlist completeness unnecessary — which is what the DOTENV_CONFIG_PATH note was trying to achieve.
findings.blastRadius: One added variable in the fixture env builder; every fixture launcher inherits it.
findings.acceptanceProof: Start the fixture API in a worktree that HAS services/api/.env; the startup snapshot must report twilio {configured:false} and getEnvSourceHint() must report no .env source.
evidenceNotes: Supporting files byte-identical on the completion baseline.

findings.codeEvidence: relationship-summary.service.ts:138 throws a plain Error rather than an AppError/validation error; evidence.routes.ts:8277 awaits it with no try/catch.
findings.runtimeEvidence: POST /v1/evidence/<id>/relationships with source == target: HTTP 500 {"error":{"code":"INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR"}}. API log: err.type Error, err.message 'Evidence relationship source and target must differ', stack at relationship-summary.service.ts:138:11, then msg 'request.completed.infrastructure_error' and an operational.alert.
findings.rootCause: A domain rule is expressed as a bare throw, and bare throws are treated as infrastructure failures by the error handler.
findings.operatorRisk: The operator is told the system broke when in fact their input was rejected, and gets no message describing what to change.
findings.securityRisk: None. The alert noise is the operational cost: every user mistake pages as a critical 5xx.
findings.recommendedFix: Throw the codebase's bounded validation error (AppError / ErrorCode.INVALID_INPUT) so the handler answers 4xx, and render the message on the relationship control. NOT APPLIED IN THIS SESSION.
findings.blastRadius: One service function and its route.
findings.acceptanceProof: POST with source == target returns 4xx with a bounded code, the UI shows the reason, and no operational.alert is raised.
evidenceNotes: Observed by the Stage 2 mutation sweep against the disposable fixture; root cause read from the API error log.

findings.title: Bulk-revoking an unknown external-review invitation answers 500 from a foreign-key violation
findings.visibleElement: bulk 'Revoke' action on the external-reviewer list
findings.observedBehaviour: When the request names an invitation id that does not exist, the handler proceeds to write an audit row and Prisma rejects `externalReviewActivity.create()` with P2003, a foreign-key violation. The API answers 500 DATABASE_ERROR and raises a critical operational alert. The unknown id is never refused on its own terms.
findings.expectedBehaviour: An id that does not resolve is a 404 (or an anti-enumeration 404, consistent with the rest of this surface), decided before any write is attempted.
findings.codeEvidence: portal-activity.service.ts:41 creates the activity row using the caller-supplied invitation id without first proving it exists.
findings.runtimeEvidence: POST /v1/external-review/invitations/bulk/revoke with a non-resolving id: HTTP 500 {"error":{"code":"DATABASE_ERROR"}}. API log: prismaCode P2003, prismaMessage 'Invalid prisma.externalReviewActivity.create() invocation in .../portal-activity.service.ts:41:51'.
findings.rootCause: Existence is assumed by the write rather than established by a read, so the database enforces it and the failure arrives as infrastructure rather than as a decision.
findings.operatorRisk: A stale list — a reviewer revoked in another tab — turns an ordinary bulk action into an apparent system failure.
findings.securityRisk: Low. It is a fail-closed outcome (nothing is revoked), but it distinguishes a database error from a refusal, which is the wrong signal to an operator.
findings.recommendedFix: Resolve every id in the batch first and refuse the unknown ones by id, before writing any activity row. NOT APPLIED IN THIS SESSION.
findings.blastRadius: One service; check the neighbouring bulk actions for the same shape.
findings.acceptanceProof: Bulk revoke naming one unknown id returns a 4xx that names it, writes no activity row, and raises no operational alert.
evidenceNotes: Observed by the Stage 2 mutation sweep against the disposable fixture; root cause read from the API error log.

findings.title: An unconfigured payment provider answers 500, where the neighbouring integrations surface answers a bounded 503
findings.backendSource: services/api/src/config/runtime-secrets.ts:125 (requireSecret), reached from the billing checkout service
findings.observedBehaviour: With the provider secret absent, `requireSecret` throws `Required secret "STRIPE_SECRET_KEY" is not configured.` The throw is uncaught, so the API answers 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR and raises a critical operational alert. The same class of condition on the integrations surface answers 503 INTEGRATIONS_DISABLED with reason feature_flag_off — a bounded refusal the UI renders honestly.
findings.expectedBehaviour: A provider that is not configured is an operational state with a bounded code, not an internal error. Both providers should refuse the way integrations already do.
findings.codeEvidence: runtime-secrets.ts:125 throws a plain Error; the checkout route has no catch that maps it to a bounded response. Contrast: the integrations routes return 503 {code: INTEGRATIONS_DISABLED, reason: feature_flag_off}.
findings.runtimeEvidence: POST /v1/billing/credits/checkout/stripe and .../paypal both returned 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, each followed by msg 'request.completed.infrastructure_error' and an operational.alert. API log carries err.message 'Required secret "STRIPE_SECRET_KEY" is not configured.' with the stack at runtime-secrets.ts:125:11.
findings.rootCause: Two conventions for the same class of condition: a feature flag refuses politely, a missing secret throws.
findings.operatorRisk: In Production the secret is configured, so this exact 500 is not expected there. The finding is the SHAPE: any environment missing the secret — a new region, a rotated key, a misconfigured deploy — turns every checkout into a 500 and a critical page, instead of a bounded 'payments unavailable'.
findings.securityRisk: None; the secret's value is not disclosed, only its name.
findings.recommendedFix: Catch the missing-secret condition at the checkout boundary and answer with the same bounded shape the integrations surface uses. NOT APPLIED IN THIS SESSION.
findings.blastRadius: Two checkout routes; audit other requireSecret callers on request paths.
findings.acceptanceProof: With the secret removed, checkout returns a bounded 4xx/503 naming the unavailable provider and raises no critical alert.
evidenceNotes: Observed by the Stage 2 mutation sweep against the disposable fixture; root cause read from the API error log.

ownerDecisions.question: Is /admin the PLATFORM console, or the ADMINISTRATIVE console?
ownerDecisions.currentBehaviour: 47 routes sit under /admin behind requiredActiveSpace PLATFORM_ADMIN. 25 are platform-only at runtime, 11 are purely tenant administration of the operator's own active workspace, 8 have no param-free GET to classify this way, and 3 are inconclusive. Every one of the 11 already carries an explicit WORKSPACE chip in the console navigation and an on-page notice reading 'Workspace-scoped surface. This page administers your own active workspace — not the platform.'
ownerDecisions.optionA: Move the 11 tenant pages out of /admin into the workspace/organization families (e.g. /security-center/*, /organizations/:id/admin/*). /admin then means the platform, without exception.
ownerDecisions.optionB: Keep them and give each a tenant selector, so /admin means 'the platform, or a customer tenant I have explicitly chosen'. This is the only option that makes them useful to a platform operator who is not a member of the customer workspace — today they answer 404 for exactly that person.
ownerDecisions.optionC: Keep them exactly as they are and rely on the WORKSPACE chip plus the scope notice, accepting that they administer only the operator's own workspace.
ownerDecisions.securityTradeoff: A is neutral-to-positive: the API is already tenant-gated, and the capability is already reachable outside /admin via /security-center/sso, so moving does not widen anything. B widens materially — it requires cross-tenant identity administration, which does not exist today and would need its own authority, step-up and audit design. C changes nothing.
ownerDecisions.uxTradeoff: A gives one home per capability. B is the only option that delivers what the URL currently promises. C leaves an operator reading 'Platform admin' above a page that administers their own workspace — mitigated but not removed by the notice.
ownerDecisions.operationalTradeoff: A is a route move plus redirects and navigation updates. B is a feature. C is free.
ownerDecisions.recommendation: Option A. The disposition register's stated reason for keeping them ('the platform gate is currently STRICTER than the API and moving it would widen the audience') is obsolete: /security-center/sso already exposes the same endpoint to every SECURITY_CENTER_VIEW holder, and both org-owner and workspace-admin hold it. Keeping the pages under /admin therefore restricts nothing and costs comprehension. Option B is defensible only if cross-tenant identity administration is genuinely wanted as a product.
ownerDecisions.approvalQuestion: Do we move the eleven workspace-scoped pages out of /admin (A), build a tenant selector so they become genuinely cross-tenant (B), or accept the current labelled state (C)?

ownerDecisions.question: Should a VIEWER be able to read SSO configuration and the identity audit timeline?
ownerDecisions.currentBehaviour: packages/shared/src/permissions.ts grants identity.org_policy.read to ADMIN, REVIEWER and VIEWER. Because /v1/admin/identity/providers and /v1/admin/identity/timeline default to that permission, the read-only fixture persona receives 200 on both.
ownerDecisions.optionA: Keep it. A read-only auditor arguably should see identity policy and the identity audit trail — that is what an auditor is for.
ownerDecisions.optionB: Narrow the two reads to a dedicated identity.audit.read / identity.sso.read held by ADMIN and an explicit auditor role, leaving VIEWER without them.
ownerDecisions.securityTradeoff: A exposes the IdP configuration (entity IDs, endpoints, allowed domains, certificate fingerprints) and the full identity event history to every VIEWER in the workspace. B reduces that but adds a permission to the catalog and to every grant path.
ownerDecisions.uxTradeoff: A means an auditor needs no extra grant. B means an explicit grant before an audit.
ownerDecisions.operationalTradeoff: B touches the permission catalog, which is consumed by the matrix page and the access-review projections.
ownerDecisions.recommendation: Option A, deliberately and in writing. The grant is already explicit in the catalog rather than accidental, the projection carries no secret material, and the surfaces are read-only. This should be recorded as a decision rather than left to be rediscovered as a finding.
ownerDecisions.approvalQuestion: Do we confirm that VIEWER legitimately holds identity.org_policy.read, or narrow it?

ownerDecisions.question: Should the Organization Admin console be reachable for a personal workspace?
ownerDecisions.currentBehaviour: Every user's personal workspace exists as a row in `organizations` with an ORG_OWNER membership for that user. /organizations/:id/admin/** — a 19-page Enterprise console — therefore resolves and returns data for a personal workspace; only the Enterprise-gated parts (e.g. /domains) refuse, with a clean 402 ENTERPRISE_FEATURE_REQUIRED and an upgradeCta.
ownerDecisions.optionA: Keep it: the console degrades honestly, showing one member, one workspace and 402 on Enterprise features.
ownerDecisions.optionB: Hide the organization-admin family for organizations whose kind is a personal workspace, and route those users to /settings.
ownerDecisions.securityTradeoff: Neither option changes authorization; the organization gate already holds.
ownerDecisions.uxTradeoff: A presents a 19-page enterprise console to a single-seat personal user, most of it empty or upgrade-gated. B keeps the personal experience small.
ownerDecisions.operationalTradeoff: B needs a reliable personal-vs-organization discriminator on the organization row.
ownerDecisions.recommendation: Option B for navigation, Option A for direct URLs — do not advertise the console to personal workspaces, but let a direct link keep working and refuse honestly, which it already does.
ownerDecisions.approvalQuestion: Do we hide the organization-admin family from personal workspaces in navigation?

ownerDecisions.question: Should Resolve be offered for conditions that cannot be resolved by hand?
ownerDecisions.currentBehaviour: The Resolve button appears for every OPEN or ACKNOWLEDGED condition. For a WORKER 'Unclassified security signal' the server refuses with 409 CONDITION_NOT_DIRECTLY_RESOLVABLE. The confirmation dialog warns in advance that 'The platform will refuse the resolve if the condition's own source still reports it as live.'
ownerDecisions.optionA: Keep the button and fix its refusal message (PV-OPS-001). Offering it and refusing honestly keeps one code path and one authority.
ownerDecisions.optionB: Hide or disable Resolve for condition types whose resolutionAuthority is not OPERATOR_DECISION or SOURCE_TRUTH, with read-only guidance instead.
ownerDecisions.securityTradeoff: None; hiding a control has never been the boundary here and the server decides either way.
ownerDecisions.uxTradeoff: A costs one round trip to learn the answer. B tells the operator up front but requires the resolvability of each type to be projected to the client.
ownerDecisions.operationalTradeoff: B needs the lifecycle projection extended to the list rows.
ownerDecisions.recommendation: Option A. The refusal is already correct, audited and specific; the only real defect is the message, which is PV-OPS-001. Option B is worth doing later if the list projection grows a resolvability field anyway.
ownerDecisions.approvalQuestion: Do we keep Resolve universally offered with an accurate refusal, or gate it on projected resolvability?

ownerDecisions.question: Should an authenticator app satisfy step-up, or must it be SMS/WhatsApp?
ownerDecisions.currentBehaviour: Step-up resolves only CONTACT_FACTOR_KINDS = ['SMS','WHATSAPP']. A verified TOTP factor — the only kind /v1/identity/mfa/enroll/start issues — does not satisfy it, and the refusal tells the holder to enrol a device they already have.
ownerDecisions.optionA: Accept TOTP for step-up. The factor is already enrolled, verified and stronger than SMS.
ownerDecisions.optionB: Keep SMS/WhatsApp only, but fix the refusal to name the required kind and link to contact-factor enrolment.
ownerDecisions.optionC: Keep SMS/WhatsApp for the highest tier of action and accept TOTP for the rest, declared per purpose.
ownerDecisions.securityTradeoff: A removes a hard dependency on SMS, the weakest common second factor, for the most privileged actions. B leaves that dependency in place. C is the most precise and the most work.
ownerDecisions.uxTradeoff: Today an enterprise that forbids SMS cannot use any sensitive control, and the error message misdirects.
ownerDecisions.operationalTradeoff: A needs the challenge flow to verify a TOTP code instead of sending one; the verification service is already abstracted.
ownerDecisions.recommendation: Option A, with Option B's copy fix shipped first because it is a one-line change that stops misdirecting people today.
ownerDecisions.approvalQuestion: Do we accept TOTP as a step-up factor, or keep step-up on SMS/WhatsApp and fix only the refusal message?

ownerDecisions.question: Should ORG_SECURITY_ADMIN be able to manage verified domains?
ownerDecisions.currentBehaviour: GET /v1/orgs/:id/domains returns 200 for ORG_OWNER and ORG_ADMIN and 403 for ORG_SECURITY_ADMIN, ORG_AUDITOR and ORG_MEMBER. Domain verification is the control that decides which email domains SSO and JIT provisioning will trust.
ownerDecisions.optionA: Grant ORG_SECURITY_ADMIN read and write on domains — it is an identity-security control and that is the role's job.
ownerDecisions.optionB: Grant read only, keeping the write with ORG_ADMIN.
ownerDecisions.optionC: Leave as is; domains are an ownership concern.
ownerDecisions.securityTradeoff: A puts the control with the role accountable for it. C means the security admin cannot see which domains are trusted for automatic provisioning, which is a gap in exactly their remit.
ownerDecisions.uxTradeoff: Today the role named for security is refused the SSO trust surface.
ownerDecisions.recommendation: Option B at minimum: a security admin who cannot READ the verified-domain list cannot audit JIT provisioning. Option A if the role is meant to own SSO end to end.
ownerDecisions.approvalQuestion: Does ORG_SECURITY_ADMIN get read, read+write, or no access to organization domains?
